identifying factors that can be used to enhance implementation of the SAFE Strategy in low resource settings and to identify gaps in knowledge that can be used in future implementation research.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SAFE strategy is feasible and can be implemented in low resource settings if it is well adapted to the local setting, and the local community and health workers are engaged in its implementation.
a combination of factors at the outer, inner and individual levels are important for the implementation of the WHO SAFE strategy for trichiasity.
the SAFE strategy has been implemented with success in different countries, but the factors that have facilitated or impeded implementation are not yet clear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the implementation of trachoma programmes in low resource settings can be improved by: 1) adapting the SAFE strategy to suit the local context, 2) engaging stakeholders and communities, 3) providing ongoing training, 4) providing resources, and 5) ensuring strong multisectoral collaborations.
a multi-faceted approach to the implementation of SAFE strategy would be more successful than a single strategy.
the implementation of trachoma programmes should be guided by a thorough assessment of the local setting and the community needs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SAFE strategy can be effectively implemented in low resource settings if the determinants of implementation are well understood and addressed.
the SAFE strategy can be implemented in resource poor settings if there is strong leadership and community engagement.
there is need for a more systematic approach to implementation research in trachoma.
